processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingots of nominal composition Fe-35Mn-19Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.

processing_steps.reduction_ratio: rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Homogenized ingots hot-rolled into plates of 4 mm thickness.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm^3 samples using electrical discharge machining for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching.
Solution-treated sample aged at 600 °C (within the 525–650 °C aging window) for 6 h, followed by water quenching. This is the defining process of this sample.
Samples for Vickers hardness, XRD, SEM and EBSD were prepared by electrolytically polishing using a mixture of 10 % perchloric acid and 90 % ethanol.

structures.overall_structure: β-Mn matrix formed by an essentially complete α → β-Mn transformation, with abundant fine BCC and FCC Cu-rich precipitates distributed at/within the β-Mn; for the 19Al alloy at 600 °C and above the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn after just 1 h of aging

interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase
interfaces.interface_notes: The content of the FCC Cu-rich phase between β-Mn interfaces gradually decreased with increasing Al content, which together with the increase in BCC phase reduced fracture toughness of the ultra-hard alloys.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness measured on an HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester with a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the hardness given as the average of 5 measurements.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: load 9.8 N for 15 s; 5 measurements averaged; specimen 10 × 5 × 2 mm^3, electrolytically polished (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol)
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure Vickers hardness of the aged samples (feeds Table 4 / hardness contour plots of Fig. 2)
characterization_methods.key_findings: 19Al aged at 600 °C for 6 h gives 895.3 ± 16.2 HV; 600 °C is the optimal aging temperature for 19Al (~900-920 HV)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: electrolytically polished surfaces; 50 µm main-panel scale bars with 10 µm insets (Fig. 9)
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn and β-Mn) in aged samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fig. 9 includes a 600 °C - 6 h panel (β-Mn matrix with magenta 'New precipitates' arrows); confirms almost complete α→β-Mn with fine precipitates for the 19Al alloy at ≥600 °C

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: scanning step size 1.5 µm (low magnification) and 0.05 µm (high magnification)
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine phase constitution and α → β-Mn transformation plus new BCC/FCC precipitates
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 19Al alloy, EBSD of the 600 °C/3 h condition shows an almost uniformly green (β-Mn) phase map with small 'New FCC phase' particles; the 650 °C/6 h condition shows a β-Mn matrix with fine 'New BCC phase' particles; the solution-treated state is single-phase α (BCC)

characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phase compositions of the alloys
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 19Al alloy the XRD trace shown (550 °C × 6 h) contains α/D0₃ together with both α-Mn and β-Mn reflections (α-Mn and β-Mn co-precipitated before the α matrix fully transformed to β-Mn)

characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with SAED and EDS
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Talos F200X microscope equipped with an EDS detector, operated at 200 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: mechanically ground to ~90 µm foils, punched to 3 mm diameter, ion thinned
characterization_methods.purpose: Elucidate microstructure of ultra-hard samples (FCC Cu-rich phase, FCC twins, β-Mn)
characterization_methods.key_findings: TEM was performed on the 15Al alloy aged at 600 °C for 6 h and the 17Al alloy aged at 575 °C for 6 h; not performed on the 19Al 600 °C/6 h sample

unmapped_findings: Elastic modulus used for the 19Al alloy in the indentation fracture-toughness analysis was E = 181 GPa, measured through compressive stress-strain curves (b0023); this is an alloy-level value and not explicitly tied to the 600 °C/6 h heat-treatment state.

Fracture toughness (K_IC) by indentation was measured only on the peak-hardness samples. The hardest 19Al sample (600 °C for 10 h, 917.8 HV) had an average crack length of 35 μm and K_IC = 3.5 MPa·m^1/2 (b0021, b0061). These value do NOT correspond to the 19Al 600 °C/6 h sample.

Nanoindentation was performed on the hardest samples: 15Al aged 600 °C/6 h, 17Al aged 575 °C/6 h and 19Al aged 600 °C/10 h (b0066). For the 19Al (600 °C/10 h) sample the overall average nanoindentation hardness was 10.4 ± 1.3 GPa and the intrinsic β-Mn hardness was 12.5 ± 0.4 GPa (b0060). These are not for the 600 °C/6 h sample.
SEM-EDS composition of β-Mn in the hardest 19Al sample (600 °C/10 h): Mn 36.2 at.%, Al 17.5 at.%, Cu 2.6 at.% (figure_014, b0060). Not for the 600 °C/6 h sample.

For 19Al, EBSD of the 600 °C/3 h condition (close to but not identical to the 6 h sample) showed an almost uniformly β-Mn phase map with small 'New FCC phase' particles, and the 650 °C/6 h condition showed a β-Mn matrix with 'New BCC phase' particles (figure_006, b0047).
The XRD pattern reported for the 19Al alloy (Fig. 10) corresponds to 19Al aged at 550 °C for 6 h, not to the 600 °C/6 h sample (figure_010, b0051).
The 19Al alloy (Fe 41.6, Mn 34.8, Al 18.6, Cu 5.0 at.%) density was measured by Archimedes method as 6.66 g·cm^-3 (b0017, b0013).
The α→β-Mn transformation in the 19Al alloy required 10 h at 550 °C, but at 600 °C and above the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn after just 1 h of aging (b0053, b0065).
Indentation Vickers cracking (used for toughness evaluation) occurred because the ultra-high hardness decreased toughness; the average crack length for the 19Al hardest sample was 35 μm (b0061).

The fracture toughness of the ultra-hard Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels decreased with increasing Al content (15Al 8.6, 17Al 6.6, 19Al 3.5 MPa·m^1/2), attributed to the increased intrinsic β-Mn hardness and the decreased ductile FCC Cu-rich phase (b0061, b0069).
